extracted.intended_audience: applicants, patent attorneys/representatives, and EPO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Overview page describing the European Patent Office's Guidelines for Examination (EPC Guidelines): their purpose, structure, formats, revision cycle and consultation process for examination of European patent applications and patents under the EPC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose: instructions on practice and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The Guidelines for Examination in the EPO (EPC Guidelines) give instructions on the practice and procedure to be followed in the various aspects of the examination of European applications and patents in accordance with the European Patent Convention and its Implementing Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This frames the Guidelines as mandatory practice/procedure guidance for how examination should be carried out under the EPC and Implementing Regulations (i.e., they are the authoritative procedural/interpretive reference for EPO examination work and for parties interacting with the Office).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope / structure: nine parts covering the patent grant process
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPC Guidelines are structured into nine parts covering every aspect of the patent grant process, including opposition, limitation and revocation procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Guidelines' scope is comprehensive for grant, post-grant and adversarial procedures at the EPO; the page also notes that all parts and indexes can be accessed via the Guidelines web page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing: alphabetical keyword index and CII index
rubrics_metrics.description: The Guidelines feature an alphabetical keyword index, an index dedicated to computer-implemented inventions and a list of the sections amended in the 2026 edition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special-purpose indexes (notably for computer-implemented inventions) are provided to help users find relevant Sections; the page highlights that amended sections for the edition are listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication formats and language availability
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPC Guidelines are published in electronic form only and accessible free of charge in the three official languages of the EPO (English, French and German).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Available formats: HTML version and PDF files (clean copy and a version showing all modifications). This affects how users access and cite guidance and which language versions to consult.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show modifications feature for tracking amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Select 'Show modifications' to view amendments. The 'Show modifications' check box is disabled for unamended sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users can view changes between editions or amendments via the UI or download a PDF version that shows modifications; unamended sections will not show modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback / public consultation process
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPO invites users to provide feedback on the most recent edition of the EPC Guidelines in a public consultation each spring; further suggestions for additions or improvements are welcome at any time of the year and may be sent to [email protected].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders (applicants, representatives, national offices, public) can submit comments during the annual consultation or at any time; the invitation implies that user input can influence future guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision cycle and update practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPC Guidelines are revised annually to keep them aligned with the latest legal and procedural developments and to improve their content on the basis of feedback received in the course of the annual public user consultation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revisions are discussed with the SACEPO Working Party on Guidelines, which meets twice a year; reports of the meetings are published under 'Updates on the Guidelines revision cycle'. This documents how and how often guidance is updated and where to find change records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation and governance: SACEPO involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: All comments are discussed with the SACEPO Working Party on Guidelines, which meets twice a year to come to an agreement on the suggested updates and clarifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates the governance mechanism used to vet and agree changes to the Guidelines (SACEPO), and that meeting reports are published—relevant for understanding the consultative legitimacy of changes.
